takeaways.label: Strong H1, guidance held
takeaways.text: Consolidated revenue grew 22% YoY to INR 195 Cr. in Q2, and management reaffirmed the full-year INR 875 Cr. revenue target despite transit-time headwinds.

takeaways.label: Order book is the engine
takeaways.text: Consolidated order book stands at INR 955 Cr., with international markets contributing INR 625 Cr. and the mix shifting from 75:25 India:US toward 50:50.

takeaways.label: Profitability snapped back
takeaways.text: H1 EBITDA grew 75% YoY and PAT grew 239% YoY, driven by operating leverage and gross margin improvement; management is targeting 21–23% EBITDA margins over time as international businesses scale.

takeaways.label: A ₹46 crore spillover masks even stronger momentum
takeaways.text: Revenue recognition rules pushed roughly INR 46 Cr. of dispatched orders into Q3, meaning the reported quarter understates the underlying execution pace.

watch.label: What to watch next quarter
watch.text: Whether the INR 46 Cr. spillover converts cleanly, the pace of Jash Process Equipment’s order-book rebuild, and any update on the US plant contract award and the parked Saudi Arabia plan.

points.label: Q2 consolidated revenue
points.text: grew 22% YoY to INR 195 Cr., driven by strong order book and execution across geographies.

points.label: H1 profitability surge
points.text: saw EBITDA grow 75% YoY to INR 42 Cr. and PAT grow 239% YoY, reflecting operating leverage and improved gross margins.

points.label: Gross margin range
points.text: is 55–60% historically, with FY2026 around 57%; half-yearly margins can vary with order mix, but management is confident the full-year range will be sustained.

points.label: Employee cost
points.text: as a percentage of revenue appears elevated in H1 because a major portion of revenue comes in H2; on a full-year basis it normally runs ~18%, rising to 19.5% last year only because the revenue target was missed.

points.label: A tariff refund
points.text: of USD 0.54 million was booked in Q2 P&L within the consumption item, providing a small tailwind.

points.label: Revenue recognition timing
points.text: depressed reported Q2 and H1 numbers: approximately INR 46 Cr. of dispatched and invoiced orders could not be recognized because destination-based delivery terms mean title transfers only when material reaches the customer, and the material was still in transit at September closing. That spillover carries into Q3.

quotes.text: Sanjay Sharma: "At the September closing, we had approximately INR 46 crore of such orders. ... Most of our orders are on destination-based terms, which means the material has to reach the customer's location before the title gets transferred and we can recognize the revenue."

points.label: Consolidated order book
points.text: stands at INR 955 Cr., with INR 625 Cr. from international markets and INR 330 Cr. domestic; the business mix has shifted from 75:25 or 70:30 (India:US) to closer to 50:50.

points.label: Near-term order book target
points.text: is INR 1,000–1,200 Cr., with management expecting to cross INR 1,150 Cr. in the near term for the pending consolidated order book.

points.label: Full-year order booking
points.text: of around INR 1,000 Cr. is possible, though month-to-month numbers will be lumpy given the project-based nature of the business; this translates to a monthly run rate of around INR 90 Cr.

points.label: Q3 revenue visibility
points.text: is strong: October standalone revenue was ~₹56 Cr., and the quarter will benefit from the INR 46 Cr. spillover plus ongoing business.

points.label: Data-centre vessel orders
points.text: are being taken opportunistically: a first order for 4 vessels was booked last quarter, and another order for 9 vessels was received in the current period; management will target 20–30 vessels per year but only when spare manufacturing capacity exists, since the segment is highly competitive and largely involves fabricated products.

quotes.text: Dharmendra Jain: "As we clearly informed investors in the last quarter, data-centre orders are not our primary focus because this segment is highly competitive and largely involves fabricated products. So, we will take such orders only if we have spare manufacturing capacity available."

points.label: Jash Process Equipment integration
points.text: is progressing: a few products have started being manufactured inside Jash Engineering premises in Indore, replacing the previous fully outsourced model; Jash has also adopted and inducted Jash Process Equipment's designs and technologies into its own water and wastewater products, with one such product already receiving orders.

points.label: Jash Process Equipment costing
points.text: is being aligned to Jash standards, since the acquired entity's costing philosophy was different.

quotes.text: Sanjay Sharma: "Their costing philosophy was different, so we are integrating their processes with our Jash standard."

rows: Order book healthy at USD 40 million (₹391 Cr.); confident of achieving USD 35–36 million turnover this year after last year's drop to ~USD 30 million on tariff uncertainty. Q3 and Q4 are seasonally higher.
▲ Revenue +8% to INR 23 Cr., PAT positive vs last year
Firm inquiries now coming in after earlier drags; a single order of GBP 0.25 Cr. is under discussion and likely to be awarded within the month. Pipeline improving.
▼ Revenue declined to INR 21 Cr. from INR 25 Cr., PAT slightly negative

When acquired (formerly WesTech India), the entity lost major orders, leaving very low order backlog entering the year; earlier last year it was ~INR 50 Cr., now projecting ~INR 40 Cr. Order inflow improved this quarter, and management expects a healthy order book by year-end with major orders in H2.

points.label: US plant
points.text: is moving forward: an AMC contractor has been appointed and is evaluating 2–3 proposals; the contract is expected to be awarded during November, with construction taking approximately 12 months for commissioning. Operations should start in the last quarter of the next fiscal year, with full contribution from FY28–29 onwards.

points.label: Existing capacity sufficiency
points.text: is not a near-term concern: existing facilities in India, the US and the UK can generate ~₹1,200 Cr. revenue at optimum load; the new US facility supports the next target of ₹1,500 Cr.

points.label: Orange facility
points.text: is receiving minor investments to cater to requirements for at least the next one-and-a-half years.

points.label: Saudi Arabia plan
points.text: is currently parked due to the geopolitical situation in the Gulf; a decision will be revisited by next month. The entity is 100% owned by Jash with no local partner; a location in Dammam had been identified and a consultant hired for documentation, company setup and land allotment coordination. The long-term commitment remains: management wants a manufacturing base in the region to cater to the entire MENA region, starting with component dispatch, local assembly and testing, then building up manufacturing over time.

points.label: New geographies
points.text: seeing increased project presence include Saudi Arabia, Vietnam and Thailand, adding to existing footprints in Hong Kong, the USA and the UK.

quotes.text: Sanjay Sharma: "But long term, we continue to remain say committed, and we are confident and pretty sure that we should have a manufacturing base in that region to cater to the entire Middle East region. And in fact, we would also like to cater to the North African region also, the entire MENA region from there."

points.label: EBITDA margin historically
points.text: runs 18–20%, with 18% being a fairly normal level; margins were impacted in 2022 and last year mainly due to tariffs and war-related effects, and bringing them back to normal levels takes time.

points.label: Target EBITDA margin
points.text: is 21–23% over time, achievable as international businesses scale up and as the US and UK businesses improve profitability toward levels similar to the standalone Indian business.

points.label: Operating leverage
points.text: is the mechanism: the fixed-cost base is not expected to increase at the same pace as revenue, so as revenue scales up, EBITDA margin should improve.

points.label: >20% EBITDA margin
points.text: is expected within 1–2 years, and management is very confident of achieving it; when asked if that holds even if the dollar remains at current levels for next year, management confirmed yes.

points.label: Scale targets
points.text: that unlock margin improvement: around GBP 1–1.2 Cr. for Waterfront UK and USD 50 million for the US business, both achievable over the next one to two years.

points.label: The caveat
points.text: is that abnormal global developments could have an impact, but under normal circumstances management remains confident of improving EBITDA margin as the business scales.

quotes.text: Dharmendra Jain: "Once EBITDA comes down from the normal level, bringing it back to those levels takes some time and remains a challenge."

items.title: Group revenue guidance
items.text: Management has maintained FY27 consolidated revenue guidance of ₹875 crore (Jash ₹530 crore, Rodney Hunt ₹330 crore, Waterfront ₹60 crore) and raised the FY27 PAT margin guide to 13-14%, implying ~₹100-105 crore PAT. FY28 is guided at ~₹1,025 crore, with a long-term target of ₹1,500 crore-plus by FY31 backed by ~₹200 crore of planned investment.

items.title: Houston US plant
items.text: Land is acquired and a ~$12 million capex plan is funded via ~$3 million of US deposits, internal accruals and willing US banks; the contractor award was expected in November 2026 with construction from 1 December and completion around December 2027, contributing fully from FY28. A complete US facility removes the 8-12 week shipping lead time that currently forfeits 12-16 week delivery orders to competitors, and supports the ₹1,500 crore capacity goal alongside ~₹300 crore from Houston and Saudi combined.

items.title: Rodney Hunt US rebuild
items.text: Rodney Hunt holds a ~$40 million (₹391 crore) pending order book, with the India-vs-US manufacturing mix moved to roughly 50:50 and ~70% of US-bound orders planned as make-in-America to navigate tariffs priced at 25%. Management targets ~₹330 crore FY27 revenue (up ~9.6% YoY), PAT margin of 8-9% rising to 10% by FY28, and a five-year path from ~$3 crore to $7.5 crore.

items.title: UK Waterfront and Penstocks
items.text: The £550,000 Penstocks (UK) acquisition completed in early April FY27, merging into Jash Waterfront Penstock UK Ltd by December 2026 with a ~₹55 crore FY27 income target and ~₹150 crore by FY31, supported by ~₹20 crore of infusion. Waterfront turned PAT-positive at £0.01 crore in H1 FY27 on ₹23 crore revenue, and management expects "huge growth" from H2 FY27 as the AMP8 cycle - set to nearly double UK water investment over five years - kicks in.

items.title: Jash Process Equipment turnaround
items.text: The ₹31.4 crore WesTech India acquisition (completed January 2026) opens the industrial process equipment segment, with manufacturing of key products being brought in-house at Indore to cut costs over 1-2 years and new product development resumed - one adopted product has already won orders for 18-20 machines. Management expects the order book "very healthy" by year-end and turnaround visible in 2-3 quarters, guiding ~₹40 crore FY27 revenue rising to ~₹80 crore by FY31.

items.title: Data centre pressure vessels
items.text: After a first 4-vessel order in FY26 and a 9-vessel order in Q2 FY27, Jash has offers out for 100-plus vessels, a 32-vessel order under negotiation, and quotes on more than 600 vessels at ₹30-50 lakh each. The current Indore setup can build 75-80 vessels a year (~₹25-30 crore/year opportunity), and sustained demand could bring the new-plant decision forward from FY28.

items.title: Saudi Arabia plant
items.text: The fully owned Rodney Hunt Mahr subsidiary received its commercial registration in January 2026, with all permissions in, land application filed, and internal timelines of land by March 2026 and commercial production by 1st July 2027 at ~$4 million capex. Local manufacturing earns purchase and price preference in Saudi tenders and helps Indian EPCs meet localisation targets, with first-year revenue of ₹20-30 crore building to ₹100 crore-plus by 2030.

items.title: India capacity ramp
items.text: The Chennai Unit 5 (August 2025), the third Pithampur SEZ plant (inaugurated February 2026, commercial production from April FY27), and a foundry plus gate/valve expansion commissioned in Q1 FY27 together lift capacity up to 30%, with the three Pithampur plants alone capable of ₹300-400 crore. These commissioned facilities underpin India revenue capability above ₹1,100 crore by FY31 against a ~₹550 crore FY27 target, with only ~₹10 crore of capex planned for FY27.

items.title: Singapore coastal infrastructure
items.text: Jash has submitted offers worth USD80-90 crore for Singapore's rising-sea-level program, with tendering from 2028, first orders expected 2029, and management targeting a 20-40% share of awards within an equipment pool worth roughly 10% of a ₹50,000-60,000 crore government program. Execution spreads over 20-25 years, making this a long-dated but large export stream after the Hong Kong Yuen Long barrage job (~₹40 crore) proved the category.
